newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA DOMESTIC DEBT UP TO 3.79 TRLN LEVS END-JUNE.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA DOMESTIC DEBT UP TO 3.79 TRLN LEVS END-JUNE.

text.p: Bulgaria's domestic debt rose by around 870 billion levs by June 30 to 3.789 trillion levs from 2.920 billion levs at end-May mainly due to the restructuring of the government debt to the Bulgarian National Bank, Finance Ministry figures showed.

"The domestic debt rise in June was largely due to the restucturing of the government debt to the central bank in line with the introduction of the currency board system," a Finance ministry official, who declined to be named told Reuters.
At end-June the government's debt through direct borrowing from financial institutions stood at 1.144 trillion levs against around 204.8 billion levs at end-May.

The BNB wrote off the government debt due, including principal and interest with a value date June 30 and issued a new debt to the International Monetary Fund amounting to 482.2 Special Drawing Rights, which is now held by the BNB.

The move was part of preparations to enter on July 1 the IMF-prescribed fixed exchange rate mechanism which requires levs in circulation, government and bank deposits and current accounts to be fully covered by foreign exchange reserves.
The system is aimed at strengthening financial discipline and stabilising the economy.
The lev fall against the dollar in the past month boosted by 101.5 billion levs the lev value of dollar-denominated government securities.
The lev lost to 1,718.6 per dollar on June 30 from 1,568.8 on May 30 in the central bank daily fixing used in the calculations.
The Finance Ministry placed in April $50 million of 18-month, floater coupon T-notes with the country's biggest state-owned Bulbank under a stabilisation plan for the ailing state Biochimbank.

The ministry issued last year $79.2 million of floater coupon T-bonds last year to guarantee foreign currency deposits of companies and individuals in five local banks against which the central bank has filed insolvency suits.
At end-June the amount of dollar denominated guarantee bonds stood at $55.7 million.
Bad debt bonds worth 32 billion levs and $1.8 billion respectively were issued three years ago to cover banks' non-performing loans extended to state companies before 1991.
The total par value of dollar-denominated bad debt bonds in circulation by end-June was $892 million and lev-denominated bonds amounted to around 13.5 billion levs worth.
Net sales of government securities in June totalled around minus 100 billion levs, figures showed.
This years budget envisages a minus 0.5 percent of projected nominal GDP net financing of the budget deficit from banks. The 1997 nominal GDP was projected at 16.150 trillion levs.
